items.rationale: Sections 5.2.6–5.2.7 cover necessary dismantling and refitting for access or drying. One service is estimated at €90 gross, consistent with Case 46.

Section 5.2.7 covers equipment for the necessary drying period, subject to moisture documentation. The estimate is €313 gross for the seven invoiced days, not the roughly two weeks reported in the claim.
Section 7.4.4 excludes the unexplained surcharge because no itemised materials list is provided. If substantiated, one surcharge would be estimated at €39 gross.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.14(c) allow like-for-like mineral-wool insulation where it was removed for access. One piece is estimated at €26 gross.
Section 5.2.1 allows the first charge for necessary debris disposal; this is the first of the two charges for the same waste. One disposal charge is estimated at €60 gross.
Section 5.2.6 covers levelling the affected substrate as part of making good. One invoiced unit is estimated at €38 gross.

Section 5.2.6 covers necessary rough preparation in the damaged area, provided it is distinct from levelling and separately billed labour under sections 3.5(d) and 7.4.1. At €35 per m², 2.78 m² is approximately €97 gross.
Section 5.2.6 expressly covers necessary service openings. One opening is estimated at €19 gross using the comparable hole-drilling line in Case 46.
The tiles are within the 90 × 90 cm limit in section 7.14(d), with sections 3.5(a) and 7.1.6 limiting the price to standard-grade reinstatement. Five tiles at €50 each give €250 gross.

The tiles exceed the format threshold in section 7.14(d), and section 3.5(f) denies partial payment for an over-threshold item. If allowed on a standard-equivalent basis, five pieces at €50 would be €250 gross.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.14(a) cover making good with standard sanitary silicone. The full 3.6 m at approximately €13 per metre gives €47 gross.
Section 7.4.2 allows the first travel charge per contractor per document. The single tiling travel charge is estimated at €83 gross, matching Case 46.
Section 7.4.1 covers necessary skilled labour not already included in other charges. The full 14 hours at €90 per hour give €1,260 gross, consistent with the revealed lower bound in Case 46.

items.description: Remove drywall and insulation wool in basement
items.rationale: Sections 5.2.1 and 5.2.6 cover necessary removal in the damaged basement, subject to the lump-sum documentation rule in section 7.4.4. The comparable drywall and insulation removals in Case 46 total roughly €95 gross, without a second disposal allowance.

items.description: Remove damp plaster in basement rooms
items.rationale: Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.5 cover removal of affected plaster in the documented damage area. The estimate uses the single invoiced unit at €29 gross.
Sections 3.5(b) and 7.1.5 exclude the attic work because it is unrelated to the basement leak. If it were covered, one removal item would be estimated at €85 gross.
Sections 3.5(d) and 5.2.1 exclude this second charge for the same waste; line 5 is the first charge. A distinct eligible disposal charge would be approximately €60 gross.
